principle: Preserve scientifically deliberate distinctions; improve discoverability with short explanations rather than flattening accurate terms.

terms.meaning: Spatial service outcome or area meeting a defined quality condition.
terms.risk: Users may read it as raw received power because both appear on the map.
terms.recommendation: Add a short definition near the legend or Results tab: coverage is the area meeting the selected service criterion.

terms.meaning: How far the modeled propagation extends or is evaluated.
terms.risk: Could be confused with coverage, which includes a quality threshold.
terms.recommendation: Keep the term; pair it with a one-line distinction from service coverage.

terms.meaning: Modeled signal/received-power representation.
terms.risk: Signal can be read as a binary service state.
terms.recommendation: Use Received power or Signal surface in metric-specific locations; use Signal as the concise map-layer label.

terms.meaning: Whether a location or demand point meets the selected service condition.
terms.risk: May be read as the same as coverage.
terms.recommendation: Explain serviceability as the pass/fail criterion used to derive coverage or demand hits.

terms.meaning: Named planning branch containing current inputs and Versions.
terms.risk: New users may treat Scenario as a temporary form state.
terms.recommendation: Show a short helper: a Scenario is a named planning branch; save Versions inside it.

terms.meaning: Saved immutable or revisioned planning state used as a source for Runs and Reports.
terms.risk: The active Version is not visible in the header, and Save version appears in multiple places.
terms.recommendation: Keep Version; persist its name/number and source status next to the active Scenario.

terms.meaning: An executed simulation or optimization record.
terms.risk: Run can sound like a transient button action rather than a durable evidence object.
terms.recommendation: First-use copy should say “Run: saved computation record” or similar.

terms.meaning: Output of the latest compatible computation or a selected historical computation.
terms.risk: Current and historical result are not consistently qualified.
terms.recommendation: Use Current result, Historical result, and Result out of date as explicit state labels.

terms.meaning: Human-readable planning output derived from a current or historical source.
terms.risk: Retained artifact terminology competes with the user-facing output concept.
terms.recommendation: Use Report in primary UI and reserve artifact for advanced retained-output metadata.

terms.meaning: The buildings, demand, cell, and source data used by planning/runtime models.
terms.risk: Dataset, installed pack, and static source are shown at different levels.
terms.recommendation: Label active Dataset separately from Dataset Pack and source/license evidence.

terms.meaning: The editable local set of planning cells and their profiles.
terms.risk: A new user may not know Inventory is the cell-editing workspace.
terms.recommendation: Use Cell inventory as the panel title and retain Inventory as the stage/tool label.

terms.meaning: A radio planning entity with a per-cell RF profile.
terms.risk: Cell can be confused with a geographic grid cell or demand cell.
terms.recommendation: Use radio cell or planning cell in first-use help; keep cell in compact controls.

terms.meaning: Physical or map-visible cell/tower placement context.
terms.risk: The domain primarily models cells; tower can imply an infrastructure asset not represented by the selected RF entity.
terms.recommendation: Use selected cell in RF UI and selected site/tower only when describing physical placement.

terms.meaning: Physical location hosting one or more radio cells.
terms.risk: Site and cell are not interchangeable.
terms.recommendation: Use site for placement/infrastructure; use cell for RF configuration and Run scope.

terms.meaning: Reference plan or Version against which another state is compared.
terms.risk: A baseline can be a Version, current draft, or optimization starting point if not qualified.
terms.recommendation: Always name the baseline source: baseline Version, baseline Run, or current draft.

terms.meaning: The user’s active choice in a list, map, or solution set.
terms.risk: Selected can be confused with Recommended.
terms.recommendation: Use Selected for user choice only; never use it as a quality judgment.

terms.meaning: System-generated preferred solution under the current objective/policy.
terms.risk: Users may assume Recommended has been applied.
terms.recommendation: Pair with “not applied” or “apply as new Version/branch” until the user commits it.

terms.meaning: A state produced by an optimization operation.
terms.risk: Optimized can be read as globally best rather than best under selected priorities/constraints.
terms.recommendation: Use optimized under selected priorities/constraints in details; retain concise labels in charts.

terms.meaning: Likely model limitations or confidence guidance.
terms.risk: The phrase does not tell the user whether it is a link to limitations, uncertainty, or a numeric estimate.
terms.recommendation: Use Model limitations, Model confidence, or Planning assumptions based on the actual destination.

terms.meaning: Retained generated bytes and their integrity/lineage metadata.
terms.risk: It makes ordinary report generation sound like storage management.
terms.recommendation: Keep in retained-output detail and technical evidence views; lead with Report elsewhere.

stateVocabulary.reason: These short labels are useful but need scope or source context to be unambiguous.
